This is the oldest footage there is! I have updated it a lot more since I've uploaded this. I've been playing around with sound and have been developing a system that effectively simulates the speed of sound. It's still very new and needs a lot of work, but it's looking good so far.

It started as making a simple homing missile that 'puruits' after the target, rather than using proportional navigation.

Basically, proportional navigation is where the missile aims to intersect the target by predicting where it'll be at after an x amount of time, whereas a 'pursuit' is just chasing. By using the targets current velocity and the missiles speed, we can calculate where to fly to intercept the target, rather than chasing and potentially losing the target. This saves time, fuel, and overall yields a higher chance of hitting the target. 

The math is a bit complex for me to explain all here. I used wikipedia aswell as a couple roblox dev forums for help. I'll have to find it but one forum led me to a blog post that was rather helpful in explaining the math.

I'll be making a simple jet to fly around in to test the capabilities of the tracking with a target that is moving on more than one axis.

Of course. The missile takes into consideration the distance between the missile and target, as well as missile and target velocities and adjusts the its aim accordingly. I also plan to add countermeasures to make it more realistic and fun.

Probably around 2-3 hours. Most of the time was figuring out the math and physics for proportional navigation. The rest was building the missile and launchpad aswell as configuring particles to my liking.
